column1: Detailed Diagram Analysis and Redesign Plan
Recommended authoring tool: diagrams.net. Layout guidance is designed for legibility when inserted into an A4 report.

column5: Actors and use cases are incompletely connected; “read only” appears as a use case; layout is difficult to follow.
column6: Rebuild in diagrams.net with the NutriBase system boundary centered, actors outside, all associations attached, and include/extend only where semantically correct. Replace “read only” with concrete view use cases or a constraint note.
column7: A4 landscape; Admin left, Doctor left/bottom, Patient right; group account, patient, visit, vital-sign, and diet-plan use cases; avoid crossing connectors.

column5: Flow stores the token in an httpOnly cookie, contradicting the documented Bearer-token approach.
column6: Show: enter credentials → POST /api/login → validate request → check active account/credentials → create Sanctum token → return user + token JSON → client stores/uses token as Authorization: Bearer. Include invalid credentials and deactivated-account branches.
column7: A4 portrait; vertical top-to-bottom flow; swimlanes for User/Frontend/API; decision diamonds aligned centrally; error branches return to login.

column5: Current diagram must be checked against atomic creation of Patient plus PatientSocioeconomic records and role authorization.
column6: Show Admin/Doctor authorization, validation, database transaction, Patient creation, optional socioeconomic upsert, commit/rollback, success/error response.
column7: A4 portrait with Frontend/API/Database swimlanes; keep transaction steps grouped and rollback path visually distinct.

column5: The diagram may not clearly show doctor-only authorization, active-patient validation, and validation failure paths.
column6: Show authenticated Doctor → select active patient → enter visit data → authorize → validate → save visit → return 201; include 403, 404, and 422 branches.
column7: A4 portrait; main success path centered; exception branches to the right with short labels.

column3: Activity Diagram — Generate AI Diet Plan
column5: Provider and asynchronous processing details are inconsistent across chapters.
column6: Use the confirmed provider. Show doctor authorization, patient/context collection, queued GenerateDietPlanJob, provider call, structured response parsing, status update, polling, and failure/retry state.
column7: A4 landscape; swimlanes for Doctor/Frontend/API/Queue Worker/AI Provider/Database; number long asynchronous steps.

column5: The edit/review workflow needs to preserve the human-in-the-loop rule stated in the conclusion.
column6: Show doctor opens generated draft → edits content → validates → saves approved/revised version; prevent patient editing; distinguish draft and approved states.
column7: A4 portrait; use state labels and one authorization decision; avoid unnecessary implementation detail.

column3: Activity Diagram — Send Diet Plan Email
column5: Email dispatch should reflect the asynchronous queue architecture described in Chapter 7.
column6: Show doctor selects approved plan → confirms recipient → API authorizes and queues SendDietPlanEmailJob → worker sends mail → success/failure status is recorded and returned.
column7: A4 landscape; swimlanes for Doctor/Frontend/API/Queue Worker/Mail Service; show retry/failure path.

column5: A duplicate Figure 3.7 was reported, and the broad clinical workflow may overlap individual activity diagrams.
column6: Keep this as a high-level overview only: register/find patient → record visit/vitals → generate/review diet plan → send plan → follow-up. Renumber after the detailed activity diagrams.
column7: A4 landscape; five or six large phases; no low-level API calls; use consistent icons/shapes and generous spacing.

column5: Figure numbering was incorrect after the activity diagrams; definitions/references and relationship clarity require review.
column6: Show User, Patient, PatientSocioeconomic, Visit, VitalSign, DietPlan, and relevant job/service relationships with correct multiplicities, keys, and soft-delete markers. Keep framework classes out unless essential.
column7: A4 landscape; entities in logical columns; inheritance above associations; orthogonal connectors; multiplicities near endpoints.

column5: Current sequence introduces Fortify and TOTP two-factor challenge not present in requirements, and conflicts with the Sanctum Bearer-token flow.
column6: Participants: User, Next.js Client, Laravel Route/LoginRequest, AuthController/Service, User Model, Sanctum. Show validation, inactive/invalid alternatives, token creation, and JSON response. Remove Fortify/TOTP unless implemented.
column7: A4 landscape; actors left-to-right in execution order; use alt frames for invalid credentials and inactive account; keep messages short.

column3: Sequence Diagram — Create Patient via API
column5: The sequence must match the service/repository pattern and atomic transaction described in Chapters 2 and 4.
column6: Show Client → route/middleware → request authorization/validation → controller → patient service → transaction → repositories/models → resource response, with rollback alternative.
column7: A4 landscape; group Laravel internals under an API boundary; use an alt frame for validation/authorization failure.

column5: The title previously included “via API,” and the interaction must match doctor-only authorization and actual Laravel components.
column6: Use title “Create Visit.” Show Client → middleware/request → controller → policy/service → Patient/Visit models → resource response, including forbidden and validation alternatives.
column7: A4 landscape; consistent participants and colors with D-10/D-11; align lifelines and avoid crossing messages.

column5: Captions, capitalization, numbering, and references in surrounding text have been inconsistent.
column6: After redrawing, assign sequential Figure 3.1–3.n labels, put captions below images, use one title style, and update every textual reference.
column7: Use one reusable diagrams.net template with title-safe margins, 10–11 pt readable text at document scale, and exported SVG/PNG at high resolution.

column5: Some diagram types lack a concise definition/reference, and several figures lack explanatory narrative.
column6: Add a short referenced definition at the start of each diagram-type section and a 2–4 sentence interpretation for each figure.
column7: Keep prose outside the image; diagrams should contain labels, not paragraph-sized explanations.
